title: OET Writing: The Referral Letter
summary: OET's profession-specific writing task — usually a referral letter from case notes — and how to select, organise and pitch it right.

nodes.label: Select relevant info
nodes.note: Include only what the reader needs

chunks.heading: One profession-specific letter
chunks.body: OET Writing gives you **45 minutes** and a set of **case notes** from which you write a **letter — most often a referral letter** to another health professional. It's **specific to your profession**, so the scenario reflects your real practice, and you typically get about **5 minutes to read** the notes first.
chunks.realExample: A nurse might write a referral to a community team; a doctor a referral to a specialist — both start from case notes and turn them into a clear, purposeful letter.
chunks.memoryHook: 45 min, case notes → a referral letter for YOUR profession. Read the notes first.

chunks.heading: Select — don't copy everything
chunks.body: The core skill is **choosing the relevant information** for the letter's purpose and reader, not transcribing every note. **Include what the recipient needs to act**, and **leave out irrelevant history** — over-including hurts your score.
chunks.realExample: If you're referring a patient for physiotherapy, the recipient needs the relevant condition and current status — not unrelated childhood history. Select for the reader's purpose.
chunks.memoryHook: Select for the reader's purpose. Relevant in, irrelevant out — don't copy the notes.

chunks.heading: Organise clearly with the right register
chunks.body: Structure the letter: **opening (who and why), the relevant background and current situation, and a clear request or purpose, then a professional close**. Keep the **register formal and courteous** — this is professional correspondence.
chunks.realExample: 'I am writing to refer Mr X, a 68-year-old with… who requires…' — a clear purpose up front, organised background, and a specific request the reader can act on.
chunks.memoryHook: Purpose → background/current status → request → professional close. Formal register.

chunks.heading: Rated on real-world criteria
chunks.body: OET Writing is judged on criteria like **purpose, content, conciseness and clarity, genre and style, organisation, and language**. **Accurate grammar, spelling and a professional tone** matter — leave time to **check** the letter before the 45 minutes end.
chunks.realExample: A letter that's clear, correctly selects information and is grammatically clean scores well; one that's fluent but dumps every note or misjudges tone loses marks — reread before submitting.
chunks.memoryHook: Judged on purpose, content, clarity, style, organisation, language. Reread before time's up.

recall.q: What does the OET Writing task usually ask you to produce?
recall.a: A profession-specific letter — most often a referral letter — written from a set of case notes in 45 minutes.

recall.q: What is the core skill in OET Writing?
recall.a: Selecting the information relevant to the letter's purpose and reader, not copying every note.

recall.q: How should the referral letter be organised?
recall.a: Opening (who and why), relevant background and current situation, a clear request or purpose, then a professional close.

recall.q: What register should the letter use?
recall.a: Formal and courteous — it's professional correspondence between health professionals.

recall.q: On what criteria is OET Writing assessed?
recall.a: Purpose, content, conciseness and clarity, genre and style, organisation, and language.
